newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends mixed on China talk, soymeal down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends mixed on China talk, soymeal down.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed mixed on Monday amid talk of China buying soyoil from South America and soymeal ended lower, pressued by losses in soybeans, traders said.
"There's talk China bought 50,000 tonnes South American soyoil," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
A Brazilian trader said China bought at least 16,000 tonnes Brazilian and Argentine soyoil over the weekend.
While the rumor suggested China bypassed U.S. supplies, traders said Chinese buying interest in itself was bullish and anything that took supplies off the market was supportive.
Soymeal traded weak all session, pressured by crop-enhancing rains in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul.
Conditions were ideal in most of Brazil's key soybean growing regions and growers said it had stopped raining in Mato Grosso state, allowing the early harvest to resume.
Soyoil ended down 0.05 cent per lb to up 0.04 with March up 0.04 at 23.80 cents. Soymeal closed down $1.60 to $0.70 per ton with March down $0.70 at $236.20.
On the day, ADM bought 100 lots each March and December soymeal, Term Commodities bought 200 March and Continental Grain bought 200 March and 100 May, traders said.
Rosenthal Collins sold 200 March and Dean Witter sold 200 March and bought 100 March.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought and sold 200 March and 200 May. Iowa Grain bought 100 March and Dean Witter bought 200 March, traders said.
